beat1_summary: Your best month since launch. Eight of twelve metrics improved, and the engagement side of the account came alive: saves and comments both roughly doubled into range.
work_chips: Themes: why DIY breaks, AI myths, founder point of view
Focus: building a body of work
beat2_prose: We tripled output this month and leaned hard into the founder-led explainer format that carried July, testing shorter openings to see what holds a business owner past three seconds.
beat2_takeaway: We published 13 pieces in August, eleven Reels and two carousels, nearly triple July's volume as we build the library out.
beat3_takeaway: Saves and comments both roughly doubled and moved into Spark range. Reach is still building, and the conversion metrics came down while it does.
beat4_takeaway: The "why does everybody DIY a business" Reel was the standout, pulling nearly five times the account's average views.
beat4_prose: That Reel earned 4.9 times average views and 2.7 times average saves. The direct, slightly provocative opening is doing more work than the explainer framing.
beat5_takeaway: September is about retention. There is a real library now, so the next lever is holding the business owner who finds it past the first three seconds.

goal_narratives: Awareness scored 26%, up from July. Views grew 54% to 6,759 and new followers to 30, though all three awareness metrics remain under their Spark floors while the account builds.
Engagement scored 52%, the month's clearest gain. Saves nearly doubled to 39 and comments to 29, both now inside the Spark range. Retention at 24% is the standing first lever.
Conversion scored 30%, down from July. Bio link taps fell to 2 and click-through to 1.4%, both under their floors, on a small enough base that a handful of taps moves the number a long way.
